Over the past few years, a disturbing trend has taken over the internet. The phrase “6000 mein Russian” has become a meme, a joke repeated in comment sections, reels, podcasts, and even songs. What started as a viral comedy clip quickly turned into something much uglier. Today it reflects a deeper problem in our society.

Foreign women travelling in India are often harassed, followed, touched inappropriately, or treated like objects. Comment sections under Russian or European creators’ videos are filled with people discussing “rates.” Even couples travelling peacefully have faced random strangers shouting such remarks at them in public.

In this video, we break down how this trend began, how social media amplified it, and why the obsession with white skin has deep roots in Indian pop culture, colonial hangover, and online pornography consumption. From Bollywood songs glorifying fair skin to fairness cream advertisements and viral meme culture, the conditioning runs deeper than we think.

We also look at how such behaviour damages India’s global image and why a few viral incidents are enough to create the stereotype of “creepy Indian men” worldwide. Most Indians are not like this, but when such behaviour becomes normalised online, the consequences reach far beyond the internet.
